guide_zh.overview: Open-source Rust agent engine and terminal client for Codewhale, with provider choice, tools, approvals and receipts.

readme.markdown:
**A coding agent for your terminal that works with any model.** Give Codewhale a task and it reads the repository, edits files, and runs commands until the task is done or it needs input from you. It works with more than 40 built-in providers, DeepSeek by default, and with models running on your own machine. `/receipts` lists the files it changed, the commands it ran, and the web and MCP calls it made. [![CI](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/codewhale-cli?label=crates.io)](https://crates.io/crates/codewhale-cli) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/codewhale?label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/codewhale) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/37gfS3ksug) [Website](https://codewhale.net) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](README.ja-JP.md) · [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md) · [Bahasa Indonesia](README.id.md) · [한국어](README.ko-KR.md) · [Español](README.es-419.md) · [Português](README.pt-BR.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [Українська](README.uk.md) · [Français](README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) · [हिन्दी](README.hi.md) · [Türkçe](README.tr.md) · [Italiano](README.it.md) · [Polski](README.pl.md) · [العربية](README.ar.md) · [Català](README.ca.md) Captured from a local demo session.
## Install macOS and Linux: ```bash curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | sh ``` The installer puts checksum-verified `codewhale` and its short alias `codew` in `~/.local/bin`. If your shell then says `command not found`, run the PATH line the installer prints ([details](docs/INSTALL.md#put-it-on-your-path)). `codewhale update` upgrades it.
Windows, npm, Cargo, and other ways to install ```bash winget install HunterBown.CodeWhale # Windows x64 (or Scoop, or the installer from GitHub Releases) npm install -g codewhale # wraps the same release binaries cargo install codewhale-cli --locked # build from crates.io ``` Prebuilt binaries cover Linux, macOS, and Windows on x64 and arm64. Nix, Homebrew on Linux, Android/Termux (preview), and manual downloads are in the [installation guide](docs/INSTALL.md), and containers in [Docker](docs/DOCKER.md). Stick to one install method per machine; otherwise two copies end up on `PATH` and whichever comes first wins.
## Quickstart 1. Commit or stash your work, then run `codewhale` from the root of a git repository. By default it applies file edits there without asking and shows you the diff. 2. Run `/provider` (or press `F3`), pick a provider, paste its API key, and choose a model. DeepSeek is the default provider. With no key, pick a local runtime instead. If no provider is configured and Ollama is already serving a chat model, Codewhale uses it automatically. 3. Type a task: ```text Fix the failing tests and explain what changed. ``` Read-only commands run straight away. For any other shell command Codewhale asks first: `y` runs it once, `a` allows commands like it for the rest of the conversation, `n` refuses. `/undo` reverts your last request and its file changes. `/help` lists commands and keys. For scripts and CI, `codewhale exec` runs one task without the interface. With `--auto` it edits files and runs shell commands without asking, so give it a container or a throwaway checkout: ```bash codewhale exec --auto "fix the failing tests and explain what changed" ``` ## Modes and permissions A fresh install starts in Work mode with the Ask permission. | | Switch with | Options | | --- | --- | --- | | Mode | `Tab` (when the input is empty) or `/mode` | **Plan** reads and searches but changes nothing. **Work** edits files and runs commands. **Operate** has the same access as Work, treats your request as a goal, and keeps going until the goal is verified or it needs input from you. | | Permission | `Shift+Tab` | **Ask** applies file edits in your repository without asking and asks before shell commands that are not read-only. **Auto-Review** lets rules and a reviewer model approve routine calls and refuses high-risk ones; switch to Ask to approve those yourself. **Full Access** never asks and turns off Codewhale's sandbox; repository rules and managed policy still apply. | See the [modes and permissions guide](docs/MODES.md) for the details. ## What it does ### Models More than 40 providers are built in, including Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, Mistral, Moonshot, OpenRouter, and xAI. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, and so do local models through Ollama, vLLM, or SGLang. `/model` switches models between turns. See [Providers](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Receipts and undo `/receipts`, or `codewhale receipts --last` after you quit, lists the files changed, commands run, web and MCP calls, agents started, approvals and who gave them, and failures. `/undo` reverts your last request. `/restore` rolls the whole workspace back to an earlier snapshot; because that overwrites later edits, it needs `/trust on` or Full Access. See [Receipts](docs/RECEIPTS.md). ### Longer work `/goal` sets an objective that carries across turns. Codewhale can split work across [sub-agents](docs/SUBAGENTS.md), run a [fleet](docs/FLEET.md) of agents, or follow a [workflow](docs/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING.md) checked into the repository. ### Coming from another agent Codewhale reads `AGENTS.md` on its own. Instruction files written for other tools, such as `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, load only when you opt in with `project_instruction_imports = ["claude"]` (or `"cursor"`, `"cline"`, `"windsurf"`, `"copilot"`, `"all"`) in your config; see [config.example.toml](config.example.toml). Codewhale warns when it finds one it did not load. `/import-claude` prepares an import of your Claude Code settings and MCP servers for you to review. `/plugin install` accepts Claude Code plugins containing skills, commands, agent profiles, and MCP servers, and refuses plugins that need hooks or LSP servers ([details](docs/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_COMPAT.md)). ### Extensions Connect [MCP servers](docs/MCP.md), add [skills](docs/SKILLS.md) and [plugins](docs/PLUGINS.md), and run [hooks](docs/HOOKS.md) on session and tool events. The bundled Computer Use plugin (experimental, macOS only) can observe and operate other apps. It stays off until you review its access and enable it ([guide](crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/README.md)). ## Ways to run it | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `codewhale` | The interactive terminal app | | `codewhale exec "…"` | One task without the interface. On its own it answers without using tools; `--auto` lets it edit files and run commands, and `--output-format stream-json` streams events as JSON | | `codewhale web` | A local web UI on `127.0.0.1` ([guide](docs/WEB.md)) | | `codewhale review --pr N` | An advisory review of a GitHub pull request. It posts nothing unless you add `--post`; the [GitHub Action](docs/GITHUB_ACTION.md) runs the same review in CI | | `codewhale app-server --http` | The [Runtime API](docs/RUNTIME_API.md), a local HTTP API for threads, events, and approvals | | `codewhale serve --acp` | The Agent Client Protocol over stdio, for editors such as Zed | The terminal app, `exec`, `web`, and the Runtime API share one engine ([architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)). A community-maintained [VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=HengQuWorld.brotherwhale-vscode) connects to it from the sidebar ([source](https://github.com/HengQuWorld/CodeWhale-VSCode)). A desktop app is in development; see the [product page](https://codewhale.net/en/product). ## Cost and accounts Codewhale is free and MIT licensed. With your own API key you pay the provider directly; local models need no key. The footer and `/cost` show what a session has cost when the price is known, and an unknown price is shown as unknown, never as free. You don't need an account. With one (`codewhale login`), you can keep provider keys in your [Codewhale account](docs/CONFIGURATION.md#account-provider-keys); on another device, sign in and choose Codewhale in `/provider` to use them. Signing in does not upload keys already on your machine. ## Safety and privacy In Ask and Auto-Review, commands run in an OS sandbox where the system has one: Seatbelt on macOS, and bubblewrap on Linux when it is installed. Windows has no OS sandbox yet, and Full Access turns the sandbox off. `/preview-request` shows a redacted preview of the next request without sending it. Telemetry is on by default. It sends aggregate counts (version and platform, session length and outcome, feature and error counts) with a random install ID that rotates every 90 days, and never conversations, code, prompts, file or repository names, or credentials. `codewhale config set telemetry false` turns it off. At startup Codewhale also checks GitHub for a new release; set `CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to skip that. More in [authorization order](docs/AUTHORIZATION_ORDER.md), [sandboxing](docs/SANDBOX.md), and [telemetry](docs/TELEMETRY.md). ## Documentation | Start here | Reference | | --- | --- | | [Installation](docs/INSTALL.md) | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) | | [Providers and local models](docs/PROVIDERS.md) | [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | | [Modes and permissions](docs/MODES.md) | [Runtime API](docs/RUNTIME_API.md) | | [Keybindings](docs/KEYBINDINGS.md) | [Plugin authoring](docs/PLUGIN_AUTHORING.md) | | [GitHub PR review](docs/GITHUB_ACTION.md) | [All documentation](docs/README.md) | ## Community If a provider is missing or a workflow is awkward, [open an issue](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/issues/new/choose) or [send a pull request](CONTRIBUTING.md). Contributors keep credit for the work that lands, and the [repository layout](CONTRIBUTING.md#project-structure) shows where things live. Chat on [Discord](https://discord.gg/37gfS3ksug), or add the maintainer, Hunter, on WeChat (`hunterbown`) and ask to join the Whale Brothers group. ## History and license Codewhale started as `deepseek-tui` and still reads that project's configuration and sessions. It is independently maintained and not affiliated with DeepSeek or any other model provider. Thanks to [everyone who has contributed](docs/CONTRIBUTORS.md). [![Codewhale contributors](docs/assets/contributors.png)](docs/CONTRIBUTORS.md#everyone) [MIT](LICENSE). Code adapted from other open-source projects is listed in the [third-party notices](docs/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
